negativeArguments: Not a normal caller-supplied password input or remote fixture import path.
No huge allocation, OOM, plaintext disclosure or cryptographic wrong-answer acceptance demonstrated.
Distinct from UTF8 word slicing: capacity/preallocation arithmetic versus string-boundary assumption.
findings.recommendedControl: Checked len*count plus explicit bounded fixture expansion using existing InputText::MAX_BYTES, preserving current accepted/refused fixture results; immediate capacity-overflow control uses two bytes times usize::MAX without allocating.

findings.title: Derived hint diagnostics reveal selected words and completion letters
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited demonstrated impact; no normal-input cryptographic compromise established. Required remediation is still authorized.

findings.reproduction: Create public BIP39/EFF suggestions from synthetic typed prefixes and format the actual returned Hint/Completion with Debug. Compare output with intentional getters; no production log sink is required for the direct diagnostic interface.
findings.expected: Secret-derived selected-word ranges and suffix letters stay redacted in Debug; intentional public hint/completion getters continue returning their documented values.
findings.observed: Actual public-interface probe confirms intentional getters return artwork and ork, while derived Hint::Words Debug prints Words([artwork]) and Completion Debug prints its letters ork. Exact2-disclosure assertion fails with exit101. No production log sink is shown.
findings.impact: Low latent accidental-diagnostic exposure of typed phrase/password segments. Public full wordlists themselves are not secrets; no actual CLI log, new owned heap plaintext, real secret compromise or universal JS/stack-erasure issue is shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace derived Debug with redacted manual implementations for suggestion types; keep the public variants/getters, equality and intentional visible hint behavior.
findings.requiredVerification: Tiny actual public-interface Debug red/green controls with multi-letter suffix and unique selected word; getter positive controls and existing hint known answers.

findings.title: Common phrase readers omit the raw text byte limit
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited demonstrated impact; no normal-input cryptographic compromise established. Required remediation is still authorized.
findings.affected: src/phrase.rs parse; Phrase::read, OriginalFacts::read and ContainerFacts::read; native and WASM callers.
findings.reproduction: Use the public zero-entropy 12-word BIP39 phrase. Add leading or internal ASCII whitespace so raw UTF-8 input is exactly8192 or8193bytes. Run the standalone public reader probe without Argon2.
findings.expected: The shared InputText raw-byte domain is checked before token scanning or normalized copies;8192bytes remains valid,8193bytes is refused.
findings.observed: InputText refuses8193bytes, but all three phrase readers accept both8192 and8193bytes for both whitespace geometries. The probe fails its exact result assertion with exit101.

findings.recommendedFix: Apply InputText::read once in phrase::parse; delegate typed TextSizeError through PhraseError. Keep ordinary whitespace normalization and independent password/passphrase contracts.

findings.title: Linux process-hardening test changes the shared test runner
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The observed mandatory fast gate exits101 on the supported Linux baseline, so current release acceptance cannot pass until this test-process coupling is corrected and reverified. Severity remainsLow because no product erasure failure was demonstrated.

findings.reproduction: Run scripts/check-fast.sh with one test thread. The hardening unit test executes PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 in the shared binary test process. Later allocator observer tests open /proc/self/mem.
findings.expected: The hardening test proves real child hardening without irreversibly changing subsequent tests or their safe OS memory-reader preconditions.

findings.impact: A reproducible Linux fast-test regression. The failures do not demonstrate unwiped data, and production hardening remains effective.
findings.recommendedFix: Run the actual Linux hardening/readback assertions in the existing guarded ignored child-process helper. Assert parent hardening state and limits are preserved; retain safe OS allocator reader unchanged.

findings.reproduction: In a bounded synthetic helper control, substitute a valid UTF-8 but non-BIP39 token such as aéé before four-byte abbreviation. UTF-8 character boundaries are0,1,3,5, so byte4 is not a character boundary. The earlier draft example abéé was incorrect and was rejected by independent review before report assembly.

findings.reproduction: Provide a synthetic built-in password case with repeat_utf8_hex c3a9 and count equal to u64::MAX on64-bit targets. Vec::repeat attempts2*usize::MAX and immediately panics on capacity overflow before Password::from_utf8. This is an arbitrary synthetic damaged-field control, not a demonstrated same-size bit flip.
findings.expected: A damaged built-in public fixture is refused as FailureDetail instead of panicking or attempting an unbounded expansion; the validation_fixtures module explicitly states this contract.
findings.observed: Only the count-to-usize conversion precedes unchecked byte-vector repetition. The current fixed fixture has short safe counts up to1025; no ordinary input triggers this path. Static source confirmation only at baseline.
findings.impact: Limited trusted-table diagnostic robustness and test-work bounding. No external arbitrary user allocation, real-secret disclosure, normal startup failure or actual OOM execution is established.
findings.recommendedFix: Check multiplication and the bounded fixture expansion before allocating, reusing the existing raw InputText byte domain. Preserve ordinary independent positive/refusal fixtures and normalized password limits.
findings.requiredVerification: A no-allocation capacity-overflow synthetic control observed failing before patch; exact raw expansion boundary and current published encoding cases passing after patch. No full-size KDF work.

coreJudgments.title: Logic lives in library modules
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Cipher, geometry, password review, repair, drawing and rekey policy remain in library owners; CLI/WASM delegate. Common raw phrase boundary omission remains N29-NATIVE-INPUT-02.

coreJudgments.title: Modules are objects
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Types own validated values/state and public operations; private records/getters/transfer functions reviewed. Native external ABI and fixed public data remain explicit boundary exceptions, not a whole-repository object-style proof.

coreJudgments.title: Classes where they pay off
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Stateful StandardInput, terminal/protection, allocator observer, engine and rekey/session owners justify state by lifetime/invariant. DTO serialization remains a private boundary; ordinary sealed JSON owner continuation is open.

coreJudgments.title: Independent modules
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Module dependencies/callers and sibling ownership reviewed, new input_text/search candidates leaves do not depend on frontends. Build/script graph proof is browser/coordinator-owned; no acyclic-macro formal proof.

coreJudgments.title: Single responsibility
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Parsing, facts, operations, engine, request/error identity and frontend I/O have separate responsibility. No new confirmed responsibility finding; arbitrary future extension not assessed.

coreJudgments.title: Open for extension
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: RandomSource/Argon2Engine/Progress and private serializers compose existing operations; unreleased typed Result API migrations are explicit and callers updated. No mandate to invent extension abstractions.

coreJudgments.title: Substitution
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Stand-in engines/random sources obey documented cost/input/output/refusal contracts; production engine initialization remains checked. Traits do not justify publishing test-only fake constructors.

coreJudgments.title: Small interfaces
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Public owners expose controlled getters/transfer and fallible arbitrary index/count/input methods. Raw phrase input-domain omission is the retained low boundary finding, not an allocation blowup.

coreJudgments.title: Depend on abstractions
coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: Core depends on RandomSource/Argon2Engine/Progress and typed input/facts; CLI owns system authority. Native C ABI/context and target-specific imports remain isolated.

coreJudgments.judgment: Scoped source/caller review with explicit exceptions and evidence limits; not universal compliance certification.
coreJudgments.evidenceAndLimits: ErrorCode::as_str, geometry/workfactor, coin declaration, check-word math, RepairWordCount and InputText are rule owners. Shared phrase parser misses InputText use; raw request adapters otherwise delegate. Export inventory does not prove all future duplicate rules absent.
